sections.title: Sound of letter o
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (o) /o/. It makes one main vowel sound. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. You hear this sound in the word (ojo) /ˈo.xo/, which means eye. This letter always has one single sound in Spanish.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Pull your tongue back into the middle part of your mouth. Open your jaw halfway. Make a firm circle with your lips. Push your breath out smoothly and turn your voice on. Touch your throat with your hand to feel the skin vibrate.

sections.title: Reading and spelling rules
paragraphs: This letter always keeps the same clear sound in every position. You hear it at the start and end of words, like in (ojo) /ˈo.xo/. You also hear it between consonants, like in (sol) /sol/. Surrounding letters never alter this sound.

sections.title: Common mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not let this vowel turn into a diphthong like in the English word boat. A diphthong is two vowel sounds in one syllable where the sound glides. Keep your lips and tongue totally still while you speak. Do not weaken it into a schwa at the end of a word. A schwa is a short, weak vowel. Keep the vowel clear and steady.
